raw_case_text:
A five-year-old male non-Caucasian patient presented with fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis for 5 days. His past medical history was unremarkable, with normal psychomotor development, no family history neurological diseases and no consanguinity. The patient was born and lived in Ceara, northeast Brazil, and family reported no recent travels.
After 1 week he developed tonic-clonic seizures. Neurological examination was normal at this point. Complete blood count, liver functions and acute reactants were normal. Serologies for HSV-1, HSV-2, CMV, EBV, VZV, HIV, and toxoplasmosis were negative. Brain MRI was normal. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed 15 cells, protein 16.6 mg/dL and glucose 68 mg/dL. He was started on acyclovir and ceftriaxone.
Two weeks after seizure onset, he presented with dystonia (Video 1) and oromandibular dyskinesia. On physical examination the patient was awake, his speech output was decreased, pupils were normal. Cranial nerves examination was unremarkable. Muscle strength was symmetric and deep tendon reflexes were normoactive and symmetric. One week later he developed focal motor seizures followed by decreased level of consciousness, dysautonomia, and central apnea. EEG showed extreme delta brush and valproate and phenytoin were started. He also received methylprednisolone followed by intravenous immunoglobulin with seizure resolution and improvement of level of consciousness, dysautonomia and orofacial dyskinesias within 2 weeks.
Anti-NMDAR antibodies were detected in serum (titer 1:25600) and CSF (titer 1:1024) after 3 weeks of symptom onset using tissue and cell-based assays as previously reported. CHIK serology was positive for both IgM and IgG, suggesting a recent infection. Dengue and Zika serologies were negative. CSF PCR for herpes viruses and arboviruses (CHIK, Dengue and Zika) were negative. Whole body CT and testis ultrasound were normal. Because of partial improvement (persistence of orofacial dyskinesias and impaired speech), the patient received rituximab and cyclophosphamide with good response. After 8 months he is seizure-free and has returned to school with only mild restlessness and inattention. Figure 1 describes the timeline of clinical features, investigation and treatment of the case report.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 5-year-old boy from Ceara, Brazil presented with a 5-day history of fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis, followed 1 week later by tonic-clonic seizures and 2 weeks later by dystonia, oromandibular dyskinesia, reduced speech, dysautonomia, and central apnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy boy developed 5 days of fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis, followed 1 week later by generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Two weeks after seizure onset, he developed dystonia, oromandibular dyskinesia, and decreased speech output, progressing 1 week later to focal motor seizures, obtundation, dysautonomia, and central apnea.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical and family history; normal psychomotor development; non-consanguineous parents; resident of Ceara, Brazil with no recent travel.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prodromal fever, myalgia, headache, and conjunctivitis, followed by generalized and focal seizures, dystonia, orofacial dyskinesias, decreased speech, decreased consciousness, dysautonomia, and central apnea.

objective.physical_examination: Initial neurological exam at first seizure was normal. Two weeks later: awake with decreased speech output, dystonia, and oromandibular dyskinesia, with normal pupils, cranial nerves, symmetric muscle strength, and normoactive reflexes. One week later: focal motor seizures, decreased consciousness, autonomic instability, and central apnea.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, liver function tests, and acute-phase reactants were normal; serologies for HSV-1/2, CMV, EBV, VZV, HIV, toxoplasmosis, and Zika were negative; testicular ultrasound was normal. EEG demonstrated an 'extreme delta brush' pattern. Chikungunya virus IgM and IgG serologies were positive, and cell/tissue-based assays at week 3 detected high-titer anti-NMDAR antibodies in serum (1:25,600) and CSF (1:1,024).
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI and whole-body CT were normal. Initial CSF analysis showed 15 cells/mm3, protein 16.6 mg/dL, glucose 68 mg/dL, negative PCR for herpesviruses, chikungunya, dengue, and Zika viruses, and positive CSF anti-NMDAR antibodies (titer 1:1,024).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Post-infectious anti-N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (anti-NMDAR) autoimmune encephalitis triggered by acute chikungunya virus infection, confirmed by positive serum (1:25,600) and CSF (1:1,024) anti-NMDAR antibodies, extreme delta brush on EEG, and positive CHIKV IgM/IgG serology. Dengue and Zika viruses were ruled out by negative serum serology and CSF RT-PCR. Treated initially with acyclovir, ceftriaxone, valproate, phenytoin, IV methylprednisolone, and IVIG, followed by second-line immunotherapy with rituximab and cyclophosphamide, achieving complete seizure freedom and return to school at 8-month follow-up.
